---
title: "Command line"
---

scjn has one verb, `download`: it puts a release on disk, in the package's
cache directory, so that every reader in `scjn.release` then reads off it with
no network request at all.

```bash
scjn download [--coleccion {leyes,reglamentos,lineamientos,tratados}]
              [--slug SLUG | --id ID] [--cache-dir DIR] [--refrescar]
```

The index is always downloaded. Assets already cached are matched by name and
never revalidated, so a second run costs no download at all.

## `--coleccion`

Which release to download: `leyes` (the default), `reglamentos`,
`lineamientos` or `tratados`.

```bash
scjn download
scjn download --coleccion tratados
```

## `--slug`

Only this law's tarball, by slug. Repeatable, and valid with `--coleccion
leyes` only. Not given: every law the release publishes.

```bash
scjn download --slug lfca --slug cpeum
```

## `--id`

Only this instrument's tarball, by `id_ordenamiento`. Repeatable, and valid
with `--coleccion reglamentos`, `lineamientos` or `tratados` only. Not given:
every instrument the release publishes.

```bash
scjn download --coleccion reglamentos --id 104906
```

## `--cache-dir`

The directory to write into. Not given: `scjn.cache.CACHE_DIR`, the
OS-appropriate per-user cache, overridable with `$SCJN_CACHE_DIR`.

```bash
scjn download --slug lfca --cache-dir ./cache
```

## `--refrescar`

Re-download assets already present instead of keeping them.

```bash
scjn download --slug lfca --refrescar
```

## What the developer docs' examples read

The verified examples of the [developer docs](https://legistlan.github.io/scjn/dev/)
run against two cached assets, put there by:

```bash
scjn download --slug lfca
scjn download --coleccion reglamentos --id 104906
```

The last line of a run says what happened, for example
`scjn-leyes: 1 assets in <cache dir> (1 downloaded, 0 already cached)`.
